conviction_note: Nearly a non-result. Citi has beaten its own mid-quarter guide by a wide margin for at least two quarters, but consensus already sits above the Q3 guide. The expense pull-forward and the RoTCE lift were pre-released on 2026-09-14, and the global IB wallet was roughly flat year on year, so the findings sum to +0.5 and p_up is 53 on a 4.0 move. Citi sold its last big beat (-5.3% in July), and JPM, GS and WFC print the same morning, so a sector read can dominate either way.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $2.66-2.68 and revenue about $23.66-23.76bn, from two agreeing sources: Zacks via Nasdaq ($2.66, $23.66bn, revised down over 7 days) and Hudson Labs, 2026-09-28 ($2.68, $23,756M; https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/citigroup-q3-2026-earnings-c-revenue-eps-preview). The company's own guide is mid-single-digit markets growth and low-single-digit IB growth with upside, from the Barclays transcript of 2026-09-14 (https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/2026-citigroup-barclays-global-financial-services-conference-transcript.pdf). The Zacks markets consensus of $6.1bn (+9.1%) already sits above that guide.
positioning_check: 21.0m shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 1.2% of shares outstanding and 2.01 days to cover (equibles.com, via the sweep row, read 2026-10-12). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism either way. The 25-delta skew is +2.18 vol points (downside paid, moderate) and put/call open interest is 1.01. The event-implied move is 3.76% against a median of 3.62% over the last four prints.

findings.finding: Citi has beaten its own mid-quarter guide by a wide margin on consecutive quarters. Q2 2026 was guided at IB fees up mid-teens and markets up high-single to low-double digits (Morgan Stanley conference, 2026-06-09) and printed IB +44% and markets +17%. Q3 2025 was guided at mid-single digits for both (2025-09-09) and printed markets +15% and banking +31-34%. That points to Q3 2026 markets and IB above the 2026-09-14 guide of mid-single-digit markets and low-single-digit IB.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: markets +17% and IB +44%, a large EPS beat ($3.15 vs ~$2.67-2.76), and the stock fell 5.29% on H2 expense messaging. Q3 2025: markets +15% and banking +31%, stock +3.89%. Q1 2026 +2.61%, Q4 2025 -3.34%. Beats are not reliably bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The Zacks markets consensus of $6.1bn (+9.1%) already sits about $200m above the mid-single-digit guide, and Zacks cites an average 14.7% EPS surprise over four quarters, so the street knows the pattern. If the beat were fully priced, consensus EPS would have risen into the print; instead it was revised down to $2.66 over the last 7 days, which leaves room for a revenue beat. The remaining edge is the gap between a ~+9% consensus and the +15-17% Citi delivered on the last two prints.
findings.independence: Q2 actuals: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/citigroup-q2-earnings-call-highlights. Q3 2025 guide: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/citigroup-cfo-expects-investment-banking-180251826.html (2025-09-09). Q3 2025 actuals: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831001/000110465925099097/c-20251014xex99d1.htm. Peer JPM guided Q3 IB and markets up mid-to-high teens (https://pulse2.com/jpmorgan-expects-q3-investment-banking-fees-and-markets-revenue-to-rise-mid-to-high-teens/, 2026-09-15). Against it, BofA guided IB down >10% and trading flat (https://www.sharecafe.com.au/2026/09/15/bank-of-america-flags-investment-banking-fee-dip/).

findings.finding: The negative that sank July has already been released as a number. At Barclays on 2026-09-14 the CFO quantified the H2 pull-forward at about $500m (severance, cards and wealth marketing), said it is self-funded within the unchanged $5bn three-year investment envelope, and lifted 2026 RoTCE from the 10-11% range to 'a bit above 11%' with efficiency 'a bit better than 60%'. A repeat of July's guidance shock on the call is therefore less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-14: an unchanged RoTCE target plus an unquantified H2 spend warning took the stock down 5.29% on a large beat. That is the only recent print where the guide line clearly drove the move.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a public conference statement, and Reuters carried it the same day (https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/citigroup-cfo-luchetti-expects-equity-return-11-year/). The only unpriced part is the asymmetry it creates. Q3 opex will include the pull-forward the street was told about, so a higher expense line should not read as a surprise this time. If the market had fully absorbed this, the skew would not still pay for downside (+2.18) and the stock would not sit 9.9% below its 52-week high with a 20-day run-up of -3.6%.
findings.independence: Same document as nothing else filed here. The sell side reflects it: Hudson Labs, 2026-09-28, carries the $500m pull-forward and RoTCE >11% as the standing guide (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/citigroup-q3-2026-earnings-c-revenue-eps-preview).

findings.finding: The independent IB-wallet series points to a flat Q3. LSEG puts global 9M 2026 IB fees at $117bn (+12%) and H1 at $79.9bn (+17%), which implies Q3 2026 about $37.1bn against about $36.2bn a year earlier, roughly +2.5% YoY and -19% QoQ. That is consistent with Citi's low-single-digit IB guide and leaves little room for a repeat of the +34-44% IB beats against a tough Q3 2025 comparison.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of the stock moving on IB alone. Banking is about 10% of revenue, and markets plus services and NII dominate.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as an industry series. The YoY figure has to be derived from H1 and 9M totals and is not quoted anywhere, so IB consensus may still be anchored on the strong first half. Net of the rest of the company, IB is a small slice: markets (~$6bn), services and NII-ex-markets (guided to the top end of 5-6% or better) carry the quarter.
findings.independence: H1 2026 base: https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/07/06/investment-banking-miglior-semestre-degli-ultimi-cinque-anni-jp-morgan-resta-in-testa-193.html. Dealogic 9M (+16%, Citi #5 unchanged): https://ionanalytics.com/insights/dealogic/investment-bankers-pocket-almost-usd-100bn-revenues-as-deal-making-soars-revenue-report/ (2026-10-07). This finding is a proxy that partly offsets the IB half of finding 1.

outside_window.finding: Banamex deconsolidation is expected early 2027, when Citi's stake falls below 50% after the final 1.4% tranche closed in Q3. It brings a ~$9bn CTA loss through the P&L that management says is neutral to regulatory capital and to TCE cumulatively. It is already disclosed and dated after the window.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, an NII tailwind
rejected_candidates.detail: Already reflected in the CFO's NII-ex-markets guide to the 'top end of 5-6% or better' in the 2026-09-14 transcript. Zacks says the hike has little NII impact for Citi. Folded into finding 2's context, not filed separately.

rejected_candidates.candidate: BofA's 2026-09-15 warning (IB down >10%, trading flat), read as a negative for Citi's markets line
rejected_candidates.detail: Same industry-wallet question as finding 3, which uses the broader LSEG series, and cited in finding 1's independence as the counter-signal. JPM guided the opposite way the same week.

baseline_tension: The mild positive lean cuts slightly against a moderate downside skew (+2.18) and a -3.6% 20-day run-up. The finding is not strong enough to say the option market is wrong, so p_up stays at 53 and the sizes stay small.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its July beat): finding 1 went from +0.6 to +0.5
Rule 6 (a finding that lands inside what the company already guided moves toward 0): finding 2 is a pre-released guidance item and went from +0.4 to +0.3

Rules 5 and 9 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series; size a segment finding net of the rest): finding 3 already uses the broad LSEG series and is sized net of IB's small revenue share, so it stays at -0.3
abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged (4.0, 53), so expected_move_pct stays at +0.24
